mainTopic: Second גט for a divorced couple found together, and the laws of a גט קרח (a tied גט missing signatures)
overview: The amud opens by finishing רבי יוחנן's view about a divorced couple who spent the night together. בית שמאי and בית הלל argue only if they were seen having relations, and the question is whether he meant them as זנות or as new קידושין. The גמרא challenges this from the משנה's case of a woman divorced from אירוסין. It concludes that the משנה argues even when no one saw relations, and that רבי יוחנן follows the ברייתא of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר. In the משנה, the argument is whether witnesses who saw the couple alone (עדי יחוד) count as witnesses to relations. When רבי יוחנן's two rulings seem to clash, the גמרא answers that different אמוראים reported his view differently. A new משנה then teaches that a woman who remarried with a גט קרח, a tied גט with more ties than signatures, must leave both husbands. The גמרא explains why such a גט is invalid and why רבי עקיבא lets a relative fill in a signature but not an עבד or a גזלן. It then discusses the case of three ties and two witnesses, the different versions of the ברייתא, and רבי יוחנן's rule that only one relative may fill in. רב אשי begins a proof for that rule, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why בית שמאי and בית הלל argue when the couple was seen
steps.stepSummary: Explains the reasoning behind רבי יוחנן's view: the argument is about whether a man turns his relations into זנות. If no one saw them have relations, everyone agrees no second גט is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: For בית שמאי hold: a person does make his relations into licentious relations. And בית הלל hold: a person does not make his relations into licentious relations. But if they did not see that she had relations, everyone agrees she does not need a second גט from him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the explanation of רבי יוחנן's view: the argument in the משנה is only when witnesses saw the couple have relations. It gives each side's reason, then says that without witnesses everyone agrees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Relations done for the sake of marriage can create קידושין. בית שמאי say we can assume the man meant plain זנות, so nothing new was created. בית הלל say a man would not choose זנות over a proper act, so we assume he meant קידושין, and she needs a new גט. If nobody saw relations happen, there is nothing to worry about.

keyTerms.meaning: Relations done without marriage, as plain licentious behavior
A person may treat his relations as זנות rather than as an act of קידושין
Witnesses saw that she had relations
A second bill of divorce
Everyone agrees

steps.confusionAlert: The worry is not about the first גט failing. The first גט worked. The question is whether the relations afterward created a brand-new marriage (קידושין) that now needs its own גט.

phrases.english: For Beit Shammai hold:
a person does make his relations into licentious relations;
and Beit Hillel hold:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין אָדָם עוֹשֶׂה בְּעִילָתוֹ בְּעִילַת זְנוּת.
phrases.english: a person does not make his relations into licentious relations.
phrases.notes: So he must have meant the relations as a new קידושין.

phrases.english: But if they did not see that she had relations,

phrases.aramaic: דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל אֵינָהּ צְרִיכָה הֵימֶנּוּ גֵּט שֵׁנִי.
phrases.english: everyone agrees she does not need a second bill of divorce from him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבי יוחנן's explanation of the משנה from just before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The argument is only when they were seen having relations. בית שמאי: no new קידושין is assumed. בית הלל: new קידושין is assumed, so a second גט is needed. If they were not seen, no second גט is needed according to all.

steps.title: Challenge from the משנה's case of divorce after engagement
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says בית הלל agree that a woman divorced from אירוסין needs no second גט, because he is not familiar with her. If witnesses saw relations, that difference should not matter.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: they agree that if she was divorced from אירוסין, she does not need a second גט from him, because he is not familiar with her. But if the case is where they saw her have relations, what difference is it to me whether it was from אירוסין or from נישואין?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי יוחנן's reading using the משנה's own words. The משנה's distinction between אירוסין and נישואין makes no sense if witnesses saw them have relations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason the משנה gives, "he is not familiar with her," only matters if we are guessing whether something happened. Once witnesses saw relations, it does not matter how close the couple used to be. So the משנה seems to be talking about a case where no one saw anything, which goes against רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: We learned in a משנה
And they agree (here, בית הלל agree with בית שמאי)
The first stage of marriage (engagement with legal force), before living together
Full marriage, after living together
He is familiar and comfortable with her
What difference does it make to me?

phrases.english: We learned: And they agree that when she was divorced after betrothal,
she does not need a second bill of divorce from him,
because he is not familiar with her.
phrases.notes: Literally, "his heart is not coarse with her": they never lived together, so he is not used to being with her.

phrases.english: And if it is where they saw that she had relations,
what difference is it to me if it was after betrothal
and what difference is it to me if it was after marriage?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading of the משנה given in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's claim that the משנה's argument is only when they were seen having relations.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's difference between אירוסין and נישואין, based on familiarity, only makes sense when no one saw relations. Once witnesses saw them, familiarity is irrelevant.

steps.title: The משנה is about when no one saw them; רבי יוחנן follows another תנא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts the challenge. The משנה is talking even about a case where they were not seen, and רבי יוחנן's view follows a different תנא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the משנה is talking about where they did not see her have relations. And רבי יוחנן, who said his view, follows this תנא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives in: the משנה really argues even when no one saw relations. It explains that רבי יוחנן was not explaining our משנה; he was following a different תנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, בית הלל require a second גט even without witnesses, because a couple who were married and are now alone together probably did have relations. רבי יוחנן's view, that all agree when no one saw them, comes from a תנא who reports the argument differently.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (we drop the earlier idea and take a new approach)
Our משנה
In line with this תנא

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוחנן is not being rejected here. His view still stands; it just follows a different תנא than the plain reading of our משנה.

phrases.english: Rather, the mishna is where they did not see that she had relations;

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן דְּאָמַר – כִּי הַאי תַּנָּא,
phrases.english: and Rabbi Yoḥanan, who stated his view, follows this tanna,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2 by accepting it and moving רבי יוחנן's view to a different תנא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the משנה and assigning the disputed view to another תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן was explaining the case of our משנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Our משנה argues even when no one saw relations. רבי יוחנן follows a different תנא.

steps.title: The ברייתא of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי שמעון בן אלעזר: בית שמאי and בית הלל did not argue where no one saw relations. In that case all agree no second גט is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר said: בית שמאי and בית הלל did not argue about a case where they did not see her have relations, that she does not need a second גט from him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא that is the source for רבי יוחנן's view. The quote continues in the lines that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר reports the argument differently from our משנה. In his version, without witnesses everyone agrees no second גט is needed. That is exactly what רבי יוחנן said in step 1.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא
They did not argue
A תנא whose ברייתא supports רבי יוחנן

steps.whatToRemember: There are two versions of the argument. Our משנה has בית הלל requiring a second גט even when no one saw relations. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, and רבי יוחנן after him, say the argument is only when relations were seen.

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר:
phrases.english: As it is taught in a baraita: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵית הִלֵּל
phrases.english: Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel did not disagree
about where they did not see that she had relations,
that she does not need a second bill of divorce from him,

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the source of the תנא mentioned in step 3.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's view that all agree no second גט is needed when no one saw relations.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.

steps.title: The ברייתא says the argument is only where relations were seen
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר continues. בית שמאי and בית הלל argue only where they saw her have relations. בית שמאי say a man can make his relations into זנות. בית הלל say a man does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: So what did they argue about? About a case where they saw her have relations. בית שמאי say: a man does make his relations into relations of זנות. בית הלל say: a man does not make his relations into relations of זנות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the ברייתא from Step 4. Now it tells us exactly what בית שמאי and בית הלל did argue about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 gave the case where they did not argue: no one saw relations. This line gives the case where they did argue: relations were seen. This is exactly רבי יוחנן's explanation from Step 1, so the ברייתא backs him up.

keyTerms.meaning: They argued, they disagreed
They saw that she had relations
Relations as זנות, meaning relations not meant for marriage

steps.confusionAlert: Be careful about who needs a second גט. בית שמאי say his relations can be זנות, so no new marriage happened and no second גט is needed. בית הלל say he would not intend זנות, so the relations may have created a marriage and she needs a second גט.

phrases.english: About what did they argue?
About a case where they saw that she had relations;
for בית שמאי say:
A man does make his relations into relations of זנות;
and בית הלל say:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין אָדָם עוֹשֶׂה בְּעִילָתוֹ בְּעִילַת זְנוּת.
phrases.english: A man does not make his relations into relations of זנות.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא started in Step 4 and states the case where they do argue.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's claim that the argument is only where relations were seen
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר

steps.title: What is the argument in the משנה about?
steps.stepSummary: In Step 3 the משנה was explained as a case where no one saw relations. If so, what do בית שמאי and בית הלל argue about in the משנה?
steps.simpleTranslation: And our משנה, which we explained as a case where they did not see her have relations: what do they argue about?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question about the משנה. If no relations were seen there, it needs to find something else for בית שמאי and בית הלל to argue about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, when no one saw relations, everyone agrees that no second גט is needed. But the משנה does show an argument in a case without seen relations. So the משנה must have a different case in mind.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
Which we explained as being about a certain case
What are they arguing about?

phrases.english: And our משנה,
which we explained as a case where they did not see her have relations,
phrases.notes: This points back to Step 3, where the גמרא said the משנה is talking even about a case where they were not seen.

phrases.english: what do they argue about?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַתְנִיתִין דְּאוֹקֵימְנָא בְּלֹא רָאוּהָ שֶׁנִּבְעֲלָה בְּמַאי פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that the ברייתא has given its view, the גמרא asks what the משנה's own argument must be about.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the argument in the משנה is about, if no relations were seen.

steps.title: The משנה is about witnesses to seclusion only
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is about a case where witnesses saw the couple alone together (יחוד), but no one saw relations. בית הלל say we treat seclusion witnesses as if they were witnesses to relations. בית שמאי say we do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where there are witnesses that they were alone together, but there are no witnesses to relations. בית שמאי hold: we do not say that the seclusion witnesses are also witnesses to relations. בית הלל hold: we do say that the seclusion witnesses are also witnesses to relations.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 6. The argument in the משנה is about whether witnesses who saw the couple alone together count as proof that they had relations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the argument is not about whether relations are זנות. It is about proof: does seclusion prove relations? For בית הלל it does, so she needs a second גט. For בית שמאי it does not, so no second גט is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Witnesses who saw the man and woman secluded, alone together
Witnesses to relations
These are the very same, the same witnesses count for both
We say, we assume

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the idea that seclusion witnesses can count as witnesses to relations. Step 8 needs this idea to explain the משנה's case of אירוסין.

phrases.english: Where there are witnesses that they were alone together,
but there are no witnesses to relations.
בית שמאי hold:

phrases.aramaic: לָא אָמְרִינַן הֵן הֵן עֵדֵי יִחוּד
phrases.english: We do not say: the witnesses of seclusion
are the very same as witnesses of relations.
And בית הלל hold:
We do say: the witnesses of seclusion
are the very same as witnesses of relations.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִיכָּא עֵדֵי יִחוּד וְלֵיכָּא עֵדֵי בִיאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה is about seclusion witnesses without witnesses to relations. בית הלל treat seclusion as proof of relations, and בית שמאי do not.

steps.title: Why בית הלל agree about a woman divorced from אירוסין
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says בית הלל agree that a woman divorced from אירוסין needs no second גט. With the new explanation this fits: since he is not familiar with her, we do not treat the seclusion witnesses as witnesses to relations.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they agree that when she was divorced from אירוסין, she does not need a second גט from him. Since he is not familiar with her, we do not say that the seclusion witnesses are witnesses to relations.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the last part of the משנה using the new reading. It shows why בית הלל agree that a woman divorced from אירוסין needs no second גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 2, the reason "he is not familiar with her" seemed meaningless if relations were actually seen. Now the משנה is about seclusion only, so the reason makes sense. With a woman he only did אירוסין with, he is not so familiar with her. So being alone together does not prove they had relations.

keyTerms.meaning: They agree. Here it means בית הלל agree
Betrothal, the first stage of marriage, before they live together
A second גט
He is familiar and at ease with her

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, the argument is only where relations were seen. In the משנה, the argument is about seclusion witnesses. בית הלל treat seclusion as proof of relations, but not for a woman divorced from אירוסין, because he is not familiar with her.

phrases.english: And they agree about a woman divorced from betrothal,
phrases.notes: "They" means בית הלל. This is the line from the משנה that caused the challenge back in Step 2.

phrases.english: that she does not need a second גט from him,
because since he is not familiar with her,

phrases.aramaic: לָא אָמְרִינַן הֵן הֵן עֵדֵי בִיאָה.
phrases.english: we do not say that the seclusion witnesses are witnesses to relations.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the seclusion explanation from Step 7 to explain why בית הלל agree about the אירוסין case.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה's reason "he is not familiar with her" fits once the משנה is about seclusion witnesses. Without familiarity, seclusion does not count as proof of relations, so no second גט is needed.

steps.title: Does רבי יוחנן contradict his own rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי יוחנן could limit the need for a second גט to cases where relations were seen. He himself rules that the הלכה follows an unnamed משנה, and our משנה was explained as a case where relations were not seen.
steps.simpleTranslation: But did רבי יוחנן really say this? Didn't רבי יוחנן say that the הלכה follows an unnamed משנה? And we explained our משנה as a case where nobody saw her have relations!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי יוחנן's position by setting it against another rule that רבי יוחנן himself taught.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה was explained (Step 7) as a case with only seclusion witnesses, and there בית הלל still require a second גט. רבי יוחנן says the הלכה always follows an unnamed משנה. So he should require a second גט even when relations were not seen, yet he was quoted as requiring it only when they were seen.

keyTerms.meaning: But did he really say...? This is a formula that opens a challenge.
An unnamed משנה, a ruling stated without naming any תנא.
The final law follows the unnamed משנה.
We established or explained (the case of the משנה).

steps.confusionAlert: The challenge is not against the משנה itself. It is against רבי יוחנן: two things he said seem to clash with each other.

phrases.english: But did Rabbi Yochanan really say this?!
But didn't Rabbi Yochanan say:
The halacha follows an unattributed mishna;
and we established our mishna
as a case where they did not see her have relations!
phrases.notes: This points back to Step 3, where the גמרא explained our משנה as a case where no one saw relations. Step 7 adds that there were only witnesses to seclusion.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the new explanation of the משנה (Steps 7-8) to challenge רבי יוחנן's stated position.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's position that a second גט is needed only when relations were seen.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Internal contradiction. His rule 'the הלכה follows an unnamed משנה' plus the משנה's case (no relations seen, yet a second גט is required) conflicts with his limiting the need for a second גט to cases where relations were seen.

steps.title: אמוראים disagree about רבי יוחנן's view
steps.stepSummary: Different אמוראים reported רבי יוחנן's view differently, so the two statements come from different reporters.
steps.simpleTranslation: They are אמוראים, and they disagree about what רבי יוחנן held.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. Two different אמוראים reported רבי יוחנן's opinion differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The contradiction is not inside one consistent tradition. One אמורא holds that רבי יוחנן said 'the הלכה follows an unnamed משנה'. Another holds that he ruled the second גט is needed only when relations were seen, meaning he did not always follow the unnamed משנה. Each report stands alone.

keyTerms.meaning: They are אמוראים, meaning different אמוראים hold different views.
According to, or regarding the view of.

steps.whatToRemember: When two statements of the same אמורא clash, the גמרא may answer that later אמוראים reported his view differently.

phrases.english: They are amoraim
and they disagree regarding the view of Rabbi Yochanan.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Conflicting traditions: different אמוראים report the master's view differently.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both statements come from one consistent רבי יוחנן, so they contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: The two statements belong to different reporters of רבי יוחנן's view, so there is no internal contradiction.

steps.title: New משנה: a woman remarried with a גט קרח
steps.stepSummary: A woman who remarried on the basis of a גט קרח must leave both husbands, and all the earlier penalties apply to her.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a woman was married by a second husband on the basis of a גט קרח, she must leave both this man and that man, and all those penalties apply to her.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It rules on a woman who remarried using a flawed tied גט called a גט קרח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גט קרח is not a valid גט, so she is still married to the first husband. Her second marriage is forbidden. She must leave both men and receives the full list of penalties from the earlier משנה (79b).

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה.
A 'bald' גט: a folded and tied גט that is missing some witness signatures.
She must leave this husband and that husband (both of them).
All these ways, meaning the full list of penalties taught earlier.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
If he married her on the basis of a bare (bald) get –
phrases.notes: 'He' is the second husband. She relied on this flawed גט from her first husband.

phrases.english: she must leave this one and that one,
and all these ways apply to her.
phrases.notes: These are the penalties listed in the earlier משנה on 79b.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. The previous discussion is closed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Remarriage based on a גט קרח is forbidden. She leaves both men and receives all the penalties.

steps.title: Who may sign to complete a גט קרח
steps.stepSummary: בן ננס says anyone may sign to fill in the missing signatures. רבי עקיבא says only relatives who would be valid witnesses elsewhere.
steps.simpleTranslation: With a גט קרח, anyone may complete it. These are the words of בן ננס. רבי עקיבא says: only relatives may complete it, people who are fit to testify in another case.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a dispute between בן ננס and רבי עקיבא about who may add signatures to a tied גט so it is no longer 'bald.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra signers are only there to fill the empty folds, not to serve as the main witnesses. בן ננס therefore allows anyone, even people normally unfit to testify. רבי עקיבא allows only people who are fit witnesses in general and are disqualified here only because they are relatives.

keyTerms.meaning: They complete it, meaning they sign the empty folds.
A תנא who argues with רבי עקיבא here.
Relatives, who are not fit to testify in this case.
Who are fit to testify in another case.

phrases.english: A bare get –
anyone may complete it,
these are the words of Ben Nannas.
Rabbi Akiva says:
none may complete it except relatives,
who are fit to testify elsewhere.

steps.triggerLanguage: גֵּט קֵרֵחַ הַכֹּל מַשְׁלִימִין עָלָיו דִּבְרֵי בֶּן נַנָּס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה by explaining how a גט קרח can be fixed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בן ננס: anyone may fill the missing signatures. רבי עקיבא: only relatives who are otherwise valid witnesses.

steps.title: Definition of a גט קרח
steps.stepSummary: A גט קרח is a tied גט that has more knots than witness signatures.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is a גט קרח? Any tied גט whose knots outnumber its witnesses.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends by defining exactly what a גט קרח is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a tied גט, the document is folded and tied, and a witness signs on each fold. If some folds have no signature, the גט is 'bald' (קרח), because it has more knots than witnesses.

keyTerms.meaning: And which one is it? (introduces a definition)
Its knots or tied folds.
More than its witnesses.

steps.whatToRemember: A גט קרח is a tied גט with empty, unsigned folds. Remarrying with it means leaving both husbands. בן ננס and רבי עקיבא argue about who may sign to fill the gaps.

phrases.english: And what is a bare get?
Any whose knots are more than its witnesses.
phrases.notes: In a tied גט a witness signs on each fold, so an extra fold with no signature makes it 'bald.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the term used in Steps 11-12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גט קרח is a tied גט with more knots than signing witnesses.

steps.title: Why is a bare tied divorce document invalid?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens its discussion and asks why a גט קרח is invalid.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is the reason a גט קרח is invalid?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא section begins, and its first move is a question: why is a גט קרח no good? This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גט קרח has more knots than signatures, but it usually still has at least two signatures. Two witnesses are normally enough for any document. So the גמרא wants to know what is actually missing.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
A tied גט: it is folded, and each fold is stitched and signed on the back

phrases.english: GEMARA:
What is the reason for the law of a bare גט?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the definition of גט קרח from step 13 and asks for the reason behind its invalidity.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why a גט קרח is invalid when at least two witnesses have usually signed it.

steps.title: A decree because the husband may have said 'all of you'
steps.stepSummary: A גט קרח is invalid because of a rabbinic decree: the husband may have told all the witnesses to sign.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a decree, because of the case where he says 'all of you.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the invalidity is a גזירה made by the חכמים. The worry is that the husband told 'all of you' to sign.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone who writes a tied גט with many knots probably expects a signature on every knot. So he may have told all the people present to sign. If he did and they did not all sign, his instruction was not carried out and the גט fails. The חכמים therefore invalidated every גט קרח.

keyTerms.meaning: A protective decree made by the חכמים
'All of you,' meaning the husband's instruction that everyone present sign

phrases.english: It is a decree because of 'all of you.'
phrases.notes: He means the case where the husband told the witnesses 'all of you sign.' Then the גט is only valid if every one of them signs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A rabbinic decree, out of concern that the husband instructed all present to sign. A missing signature would then leave his instruction unfulfilled.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the problem with a גט קרח is not a lack of witnesses. The problem is a possible condition the husband set.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: anyone can fill in the signatures
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes בן ננס's ruling from the משנה that anyone may complete a גט קרח.
steps.simpleTranslation: A גט קרח: anyone may complete it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the משנה to set up its next discussion. That discussion is about the argument over who may sign to fill the missing spots.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is בן ננס's view: even people normally unfit to testify may sign to complete the count. רבי עקיבא allows only relatives. Quoting this line opens the question about רבי עקיבא's reasoning.

keyTerms.meaning: Complete, meaning to fill in the missing signatures
The תנא who allows anyone to fill in the signatures

phrases.english: A bare גט:
anyone may complete it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from why the גט is invalid to who may fix it, by quoting the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to בן ננס, anyone may sign to complete the number of signatures on a גט קרח.

steps.title: Why does רבי עקיבא exclude a slave?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why, according to רבי עקיבא, an עבד may not fill in a signature.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבי עקיבא, what is the reason an עבד may not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי עקיבא rejects an עבד as a filler signer. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא allows relatives, who are normally unfit witnesses. So why not an עבד, who is also normally unfit? The גמרא wants the reason for this difference.

keyTerms.meaning: An עבד כנעני, a slave owned by a Jew, who is not a valid witness
The תנא who allows only relatives to fill in signatures

phrases.english: And according to רבי עקיבא,
what is the reason a slave may not sign?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא עֶבֶד מַאי טַעְמָא לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Following the quote of the משנה, asks about the other side of the argument, רבי עקיבא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What separates an עבד from a relative in רבי עקיבא's view.

steps.title: People might think the slave is a valid witness
steps.stepSummary: First answer: if an עבד signs, people may conclude he is fit to testify.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because people will come to say he is fit to testify.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a first reason. If an עבד's signature appears on a גט, people might think he is a valid witness everywhere.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry is about how things look. Seeing an עבד's name among the witnesses could lead people to use him as a real witness in other cases. This answer will be challenged in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: People will come to say
Fit to serve as a witness

phrases.english: Because people will come to say
that he is fit to testify.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a first answer to step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: People may mistakenly treat the עבד as a valid witness in general.

steps.title: The same worry applies to a relative
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the first answer: people could make the same mistake about a relative.
steps.simpleTranslation: A relative too: people will come to say he is fit to testify!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the first answer. If that were the worry, רבי עקיבא should ban relatives too, yet he allows them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A relative is also normally unfit to testify. Seeing him sign could just as easily lead people to think relatives are valid witnesses. So the first reason cannot explain why רבי עקיבא treats the two differently.

keyTerms.meaning: A relative, who is normally unfit to testify
Also, too

phrases.english: A relative too:
people will come to say he is fit to testify!

steps.triggerLanguage: קָרוֹב נָמֵי אָתוּ לְמֵימַר כָּשֵׁר לְעֵדוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer given in step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reason that an עבד is excluded because people will think he is a valid witness.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same worry exists for a relative, whom רבי עקיבא permits. So this reason cannot be what separates the two.

steps.title: The real worry: raising the slave's lineage
steps.stepSummary: New reason: if an עבד signs, people may think he is a free Jew and fit to marry into Jewish families.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is the reason for an עבד: perhaps people will come to raise him up in matters of lineage.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the first reason and gives a new one. The danger is that people will mistake the עבד for a free Jew.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a relative, nobody doubts that he is a Jew, so the only risk is about testimony, and that risk was not enough to ban him. With an עבד, people seeing his signature on a גט might think he is a full Jew. They might then let him marry a Jewish woman. This lineage danger exists only for the עבד, which explains the difference.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, which signals that the earlier answer is being replaced
To raise him up, meaning to give him a higher status
Lineage, the family status that affects who one may marry

phrases.english: Rather, for a slave this is the reason:
that perhaps people will come
to raise him up in matters of lineage.
phrases.notes: They would think that since he signed a גט, he must be a free Jew who may marry into Jewish families.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected answer of step 18 in response to the challenge of step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replacing the reason: a new concern that applies only to an עבד
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The עבד was thought to be excluded because people might treat him as a valid witness.
steps.terutzMaskana: The עבד is excluded because people might wrongly raise his lineage status and let him marry a Jewish woman. That concern does not exist for a relative.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי עקיבא, a relative may fill in a signature on a גט קרח but an עבד may not. The reason is not testimony. People might mistake the עבד for a free Jew in matters of lineage.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't stop at the first answer about testimony. The גמרא rejects it, because it would also rule out relatives. The final reason is about lineage.

steps.title: A robber has fine lineage, so why can't he sign?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks the lineage reason: a גזלן has proper lineage, yet the משנה implies he may not complete the גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: A robber has proper lineage, so he should be allowed to sign! Yet the משנה says רבי עקיבא allows only relatives, who are fit to testify in other cases. That means a relative may sign, but a robber may not!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the reason from Step 20. If the only worry about an עבד is lineage, then a גזלן, whose lineage is fine, should be allowed to sign.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says רבי עקיבא allows only קרובים, so a גזלן is not allowed. A גזלן's lineage is not in doubt, so the lineage worry cannot explain why he is left out. The reason from Step 20 is therefore not enough.

keyTerms.meaning: A robber, who is disqualified as a witness
Lineage, meaning family purity for marriage
They complete, meaning they fill in the missing signatures
Fit to testify elsewhere, meaning in cases that do not involve their own relatives

phrases.english: A robber – he has proper lineage, so let him be fit!
Why, then, did we learn

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: אֵין מַשְׁלִימִין עָלָיו
phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says: they do not complete it

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא קְרוֹבִים, הָרְאוּיִין לְהָעִיד בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר;
phrases.english: except with relatives, who are fit to testify in another case;
a relative – yes, a robber – no!

steps.triggerLanguage: גַּזְלָן – דְּבַר יוּחֲסִין הוּא, לִיתַּכְשַׁר! אַלְּמָה תְּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the lineage reason given in Step 20
steps.kashyaTarget: The reason that an עבד may not sign because people would think he may marry into Jewish families
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A גזלן has no lineage problem, yet the משנה still excludes him. So lineage cannot be the real reason for excluding signers.

steps.title: People might think the slave was freed or the robber repented
steps.stepSummary: The new reason: people might wrongly think the עבד was freed or the גזלן did תשובה, and then accept them as witnesses. Everyone knows a קרוב is a relative, so there is no such mistake.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is the reason for a slave: people will say his master freed him. For a robber too, people will say he repented. What can be said about a relative? Everyone knows a relative is a relative.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new reason that covers both the עבד and the גזלן, and explains why a קרוב is still allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry is that people seeing the signature will think the person's status has changed, and will let him testify in every case. An עבד could have been freed, and a גזלן could have done תשובה, so that mistake is possible. A family connection never changes, and everyone knows it, so nobody will be misled by a קרוב signing.

keyTerms.meaning: His master truly freed him
He has repented
Everyone knows

steps.whatToRemember: The final reason is that people might think the signer's disqualification has ended. The עבד might seem freed and the גזלן might seem to have done תשובה. Being a קרוב is a fixed and well-known status, so a relative may complete the גט.

phrases.english: Rather, this is the reason for a slave:
that people will come to say: his master freed him;

phrases.aramaic: גַּזְלָן נָמֵי – אָתוּ לְמֵימַר: תְּשׁוּבָה עֲבַד;
phrases.english: a robber too – they will come to say: he repented;
a relative – what is there to say?

phrases.aramaic: קָרוֹב כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא יָדְעִי דְּקָרוֹב הוּא.
phrases.english: About a relative, everyone knows that he is a relative.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the lineage reason after Step 21's challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: New reason that replaces the earlier one
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The worry was about lineage and marriage
steps.terutzMaskana: The worry is that people will think the disqualification has ended. That applies to an עבד and a גזלן, but not to a קרוב.

steps.title: The dispute applies only when there are extra ties
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה rules that בן ננס and רבי עקיבא argue only when at least three witnesses have already signed. With three ties and only two witnesses, everyone agrees that only a קרוב may complete it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Through a chain of teachers, רב אדא בר אהבה says: a גט קרח with seven ties and six witnesses, six and five, five and four, or four and three: only in these cases do בן ננס and רבי עקיבא argue. But if it has three ties and two witnesses, everyone agrees only a relative may complete it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching limits where the מחלוקת in the משנה applies. It depends on how many witnesses have already signed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גט מקושר needs at least three witnesses. When three or more have signed, the missing signature only fills an extra tie, and that is where בן ננס and רבי עקיבא argue. When only two have signed, the missing signature is one of the three required witnesses. Even בן ננס agrees that only a קרוב may fill that spot.

keyTerms.meaning: Ties, meaning the folds sewn shut on a tied document
A tied גט that needs a witness on each tie and at least three witnesses
A dispute
Everyone agrees

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up ties and witnesses. The ties are the sewn folds. Each tie should have a witness signing, and the gap is the tie that has no witness.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר שְׁאֵילְתָא
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said that Rabba bar She'eilta said

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הַמְנוּנָא סָבָא אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה:
phrases.english: that Rav Hamnuna the Elder said that Rav Adda bar Ahava said:

phrases.aramaic: גֵּט קֵרֵחַ – קְשָׁרָיו שִׁבְעָה וְעֵדָיו שִׁשָּׁה;
phrases.english: A bare bill of divorce – its ties are seven and its witnesses six;

phrases.aramaic: שִׁשָּׁה וְעֵדָיו חֲמִשָּׁה; חֲמִשָּׁה וְעֵדָיו אַרְבָּעָה;
phrases.english: six and its witnesses five; five and its witnesses four;
four and its witnesses three –

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן מַחְלוֹקֶת בֶּן נַנָּס וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא.
phrases.english: up to here is the dispute of ben Nannas and Rabbi Akiva.
But if its ties are three and its witnesses two –

phrases.aramaic: דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל אֵין מַשְׁלִימִין עָלָיו אֶלָּא קָרוֹב.
phrases.english: all agree that they complete it only with a relative.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר שְׁאֵילְתָא אָמַר רַב הַמְנוּנָא סָבָא אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: where exactly the מחלוקת in the משנה applies
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מחלוקת applies only when at least three witnesses have signed. With three ties and two witnesses, everyone agrees only a קרוב may complete it.

steps.title: Three witnesses on a tied גט are like two on a plain one
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא challenges the ruling: the three required witnesses of a tied גט are like the two witnesses of a plain גט, so a קרוב should not be allowed to be one of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said to רבה בר שאילתא: After all, three witnesses on a tied document are like two on a plain one. Just as a relative cannot be one of the two there, a relative should not be one of the three here!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא challenges the second half of the ruling he himself passed on, which allowed a קרוב to fill in the third required signature.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים required three witnesses on a tied גט to match the two witnesses of a plain גט. On a plain גט a קרוב can never be one of the two witnesses. So on a tied גט, a קרוב should not be one of the three required witnesses either.

keyTerms.meaning: After all, used to begin a logical argument
A plain document that is not folded or tied

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי זֵירָא לְרַבָּה בַּר שְׁאֵילְתָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said to Rabba bar She'eilta:
After all, all three witnesses on a tied document –
are like two on a plain document;
just as there – a relative cannot sign,
so too here – a relative should not sign!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי זֵירָא לְרַבָּה בַּר שְׁאֵילְתָא: מִכְּדֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the 'everyone agrees, only a relative' part of Step 23
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that a קרוב may complete a גט קרח with three ties and two witnesses
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The three required witnesses on a tied גט are like the two on a plain גט. A קרוב is never allowed among those two, so he should not be allowed among these three.

steps.title: The third witness on a tied גט is only required by the חכמים
steps.stepSummary: The rabbi answering רבי זירא admits he had the same difficulty. The question was passed up to רב אדא בר אהבה, who explained that the three-witness rule for a tied גט is not from the Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I found this difficult too. I asked רב המנונא, and רב המנונא asked רב אדא בר אהבה. He answered: Don't compare the three witnesses of a tied גט to the two of a plain גט, because the rule of three is not from the Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רבי זירא's challenge from step 24. The Torah only requires two witnesses, so the extra third witness of a tied גט is a rule of the חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא said all three witnesses of a tied גט should be treated like the two of a plain גט, so none of them may be a קרוב. The answer is that only two witnesses are needed by Torah law. The third is a rabbinic addition, so the חכמים could allow a קרוב to fill that spot.

keyTerms.meaning: A 'tied' גט: folded and tied, with witnesses signing on the back of each fold
Leave it aside, don't compare it
From the Torah
An אמורא who passed the question on to רב אדא בר אהבה

steps.whyThisMatters: It explains why the rules for the extra witness can be looser. A rabbinic requirement can carry rabbinic leniencies.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אַף לְדִידִי קַשְׁיָא לִי,
phrases.english: He said to him: To me as well it was difficult,
and I asked it of רב המנונא,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב הַמְנוּנָא לְרַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה,
phrases.english: and רב המנונא asked רב אדא בר אהבה,
and he said to him: Leave aside the three witnesses in a tied גט,
since that requirement is not from the Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אַף לְדִידִי קַשְׁיָא לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers רבי זירא's challenge in step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes a Torah requirement from a rabbinic one
steps.terutzHavaAmina: All three witnesses of a tied גט are like the two Torah witnesses, so a קרוב cannot be one of them.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only two witnesses are required by the Torah. The third is rabbinic, so a קרוב may fill that spot.

steps.title: A ברייתא lists the cases where בן ננס and רבי עקיבא argue
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא supports רב אדא בר אהבה. It lists the cases of a bare tied גט where the two תנאים argue, and in every one there are at least three witnesses.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is also taught in a ברייתא: A bare גט with seven ties and six witnesses, six ties and five witnesses, five ties and four witnesses, or four ties and three witnesses. Only these cases are the argument of בן ננס and רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to back up רב אדא בר אהבה's ruling. This first part lists the cases where the argument applies, and it sets up the key line in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each listed case is missing just one witness, and the smallest case still has three witnesses. That matches רב אדא בר אהבה's ruling that the argument applies only when at least three witnesses have already signed.

keyTerms.meaning: It is also taught this way in a ברייתא (a supporting source)
A 'bald' גט: a tied גט with more ties than witnesses
The ties or folds of a tied גט
Up to here, only in these cases

phrases.english: It is also taught this way:
A bare גט:
phrases.notes: 'Bare' or 'bald' means some ties have no witness signed on them.

phrases.english: its ties are seven and its witnesses six;
six ties and its witnesses five;
five ties and its witnesses four;
four ties and its witnesses three:

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן מַחְלוֹקֶת בֶּן נַנָּס וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא.
phrases.english: only in these cases is the argument of בן ננס and רבי עקיבא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings outside support for רב אדא בר אהבה's ruling, which was just defended.
steps.raayaObject: רב אדא בר אהבה's ruling that the argument applies only when at least three witnesses have signed
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא listing the cases of the argument

steps.title: With three ties and two witnesses, everyone agrees only a קרוב may complete it
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא gives the argument: if an עבד completes the גט, בן ננס says the child is כשר and רבי עקיבא says he is a ממזר. With three ties and two witnesses, everyone agrees only a קרוב may complete it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If an עבד completed it, בן ננס says the child is כשר, and רבי עקיבא says the child is a ממזר. But if there are three ties and two witnesses, everyone agrees only a קרוב may complete it.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes, and its last line is the actual proof. It says exactly what רב אדא בר אהבה said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When there are only two witnesses, the one completing it is the third required witness. The ברייתא says even בן ננס allows only a קרוב there, not an עבד or anyone else. This is exactly רב אדא בר אהבה's ruling from step 23, which step 25 explained: the third witness is only rabbinic, so a קרוב may fill that spot.

keyTerms.meaning: Completed it (signed as the last needed witness)
A child of a forbidden union, as if the woman were still married
Everyone agrees

steps.whatToRemember: With three ties and only two witnesses, everyone agrees only a קרוב may complete the גט. This supports רב אדא בר אהבה.

phrases.english: If an עבד completed it,
בן ננס says: The child is valid;
phrases.notes: He means a child born after the woman remarried using this גט.

phrases.english: and רבי עקיבא says: The child is a ממזר.
But if its ties are three and its witnesses two,
everyone agrees that no one may complete it
except a relative.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא begun in step 26 and gives the line that proves the point.
steps.raayaObject: רב אדא בר אהבה's ruling, together with the explanation in step 25
steps.raayaSupportSource: The last line of the ברייתא: with three ties and two witnesses, only a קרוב may complete it

steps.title: רב יוסף's version: only a valid witness may complete it
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף taught the ruling differently. With three ties and two witnesses, only a fully valid witness may complete the גט, not even a קרוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף taught: 'a valid witness'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another version of the rule. In רב יוסף's version, the case of three ties and two witnesses can be completed only by a fully valid witness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This version sides with רבי זירא's idea from step 24. All three required witnesses must be fully valid, so even a קרוב is not allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Taught, gave his version of the teaching
A valid witness
An אמורא who taught a different version

steps.confusionAlert: Here כשר means a valid witness, not a valid child as in the ברייתא. רב יוסף is saying even a קרוב may not complete it.

phrases.english: רב יוסף taught: 'A valid witness.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different version of the ruling in the ברייתא's last line.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With three ties and two witnesses, only a fully valid witness may complete the גט.

steps.title: But the ברייתא says a קרוב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב יוסף from the ברייתא just quoted, which says a קרוב may complete it.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is taught: 'a relative'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב יוסף's version. The ברייתא in step 27 clearly says a קרוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף says only a valid witness may complete it. The ברייתא explicitly allows a קרוב, so his version seems to contradict it.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it taught in a ברייתא? (opens a challenge)

phrases.english: But it is taught: A relative!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב יוסף's version from step 28.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא explicitly says 'only a relative' may complete it, which contradicts 'only a valid witness'.

steps.title: רב פפא corrects the ברייתא to read 'valid'
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא defends רב יוסף by correcting the wording of the ברייתא. It should say 'valid' instead of 'relative'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Teach in the ברייתא: 'a valid witness'.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the challenge by changing the wording of the ברייתא so it matches רב יוסף.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer does not explain away the ברייתא. It changes the text: read 'כשר' instead of 'קרוב'. In רב יוסף's version, then, even a קרוב may not complete a tied גט that has only two witnesses.

keyTerms.meaning: Teach it this way (correct the wording)
An אמורא who corrects the wording of the ברייתא

steps.whatToRemember: There are two versions. In the ברייתא as first quoted, which supports רב אדא בר אהבה, a קרוב may complete a גט with three ties and two witnesses. In רב יוסף's version, as corrected by רב פפא, only a fully valid witness may.

phrases.english: רב פפא said:
Teach: A valid witness.
phrases.notes: He is changing the word in the ברייתא: read 'valid' where it says 'relative'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 29 against רב יוסף.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Corrects the wording of the source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא says a קרוב may complete it, so רב יוסף is contradicted.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא should read 'valid', so רב יוסף's version stands.

steps.title: Only one relative may help complete a tied גט
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules that on a tied גט, the חכמים allowed only one relative to sign as a filler witness, not two. Two might lead a court to confirm the גט using two relatives and only one valid witness.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: On a tied גט, the חכמים allowed only one relative to sign. Two relatives are not allowed, because a court might come to confirm the גט with two relatives and one valid witness.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן sets a limit: a relative may sign to fill up the count on a tied גט, but only one relative.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A tied גט needs as many signatures as it has ties, so a relative may sometimes fill a gap. When a court later confirms a גט, it checks only three signatures. If two relatives signed, the court could end up relying on two relatives and just one valid witness, which is not proper testimony.

keyTerms.meaning: they (the חכמים) made valid, allowed
a relative, normally not allowed to be a witness
to confirm the document in court by checking the signatures
a fully valid witness
perhaps, maybe (a worry)

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוחנן is not saying a relative is a valid witness in general. A relative's signature only helps fill up the number of signatures on a tied גט.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
They did not validate in it
anything except one witness who is a relative,
but two, no,
perhaps they will come to confirm it
with two relatives and one valid witness.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: לֹא הוּכְשְׁרוּ בּוֹ אֶלָּא עֵד אֶחָד קָרוֹב בִּלְבַד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After discussing whether a relative may complete a tied גט, רבי יוחנן limits how many relatives may be used.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only one relative may serve as a filler witness on a tied גט, because with two relatives a court might confirm the גט based on two relatives and one valid witness.

steps.title: רב אשי begins to show the ברייתא supports רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says the wording of the ברייתא is also exact in a way that supports רבי יוחנן. The proof itself comes on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: The ברייתא is also precise in its wording, and it supports this.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. רב אשי announces that the wording of the ברייתא backs up רבי יוחנן, and the גמרא is about to show how.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase מתניתא נמי דייקא means a careful reading of a source's exact words leads to the same rule. Here that source is the ברייתא. The actual reading comes on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: a תנאי teaching; here, the ברייתא
also
is precise; its exact wording proves the point

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
The ברייתא is also precise,
phrases.notes: Here מתניתא means the ברייתא we have been quoting, not our משנה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Introduces support from the ברייתא for רבי יוחנן's ruling.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's rule that only one relative may complete a tied גט
steps.raayaSupportSource: The exact wording of the ברייתא (the details come on the next amud)
